# Implementation Plan: Roadmap Naming Rebrand (overview → roadmap, surface-only)
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"overview-naming-rebrand"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-27. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan .ralph/jobs/overview-naming-rebrand/plan.md`.*

## Overview

Adopt **"roadmap"** as the canonical HUMAN-FACING name for the system currently called
"overview" (the `ralph-overview` plugin's curated task board + watcher pipeline state), while
KEEPING the entire technical identity unchanged. This implements brainstorm direction **D-001**
(`.ralph/brainstorms/overview-naming-rebrand/selected-direction.md`): lead with a one-line
definition + a two-part glossary, rename only living human-facing surfaces (prose, the
bookkeeper role wording, the viewer's visible title/header, additive npm script aliases), and
add a small set of non-destructive technical aliases. The cross-machine contracts — the
`ralph-overview` plugin/marketplace package name, the `mcp__ralph-overview__*` MCP namespace, the
`.ralph-overview/` data directory, `RALPH_OVERVIEW_PLUGIN_ROOT`, the `bin/ralph-overview.mjs`
wrapper, and the `Overview*` TS types — all stay as the primary technical identity because they
live in per-machine settings / published indexes that the repo cannot atomically migrate.

This is the **surface-only (~200u) + optional additive-alias (~40u)** scope, explicitly NOT the
destructive full rename (~575u). The three schema prerequisites
(`overview-data-dynamic-stages-schema`, `overview-data-ship-manifest`,
`overview-data-context-scalability`) are all already `lifecycle: merged`, so the cheap
human-facing layer can land now with no schema/contract dependency.

The work splits across **two repos**: codexu (this repo) and the `ai-developer-toolkit` submodule
(which holds `plugins/ralph-overview/`). **Commit ordering (corrected):** the codexu docs/scripts
surface edits are independent of the submodule and can land at any time; the *toolkit (submodule)*
edits land first to produce the bumped plugin version + commit; then a final **codexu pointer/table
ship** records the new submodule pointer **and** the active-plugin-versions table bump together.
The submodule edits SERIALIZE at ship time with the sibling task `ralph-overview-create-task-skill`
(same plugin → conflicting `plugin.json`/`CHANGELOG`/`AGENTS`/skill writes).

## Approach

### Architecture
The rename is **semantic, not a blind find-replace.** A token "overview" is renamed ONLY when it
refers to THIS system. Three categories are explicitly preserved:
1. **Technical identifiers** even when embedded in prose: `.ralph-overview/`, `overview.html`,
   `mcp__ralph-overview__*`, the `overview.*` MCP tool names, `Overview*` type names,
   `RALPH_OVERVIEW_PLUGIN_ROOT`, `bin/ralph-overview.mjs`, `ralph-overview` /
   `ralph-overview@ai-developer-toolkit`.
2. **The generic English word** "overview" (e.g. a doc's `## Overview` section heading in
   `docs/backend-architecture.md` / `docs/cli-architecture.md` and similar) — unrelated to the system.
   **The test is the REFERENT, not the `##`/heading form:** a heading is renamed when it names THIS
   system and preserved when it names the generic concept. Concretely, `AGENTS.md`'s
   `## Overview data — two-file split` (≈ line 218) IS a system reference and a rename target (→ e.g.
   "Roadmap data — two-file split"); only generic-concept headings in unrelated architecture docs are
   preserved. Do NOT apply a blanket "skip all `## Overview` headings" rule.
3. **Frozen historical artifacts:** `.ralph/` history, `generated/**`, completed point-in-time plan
   docs, and historical CHANGELOG entries (they describe past releases that genuinely shipped under
   the "overview" name; rewriting them falsifies history). New CHANGELOG entries use current wording.

**Two-part canonical vocabulary** (the glossary that ships first):
- **roadmap** = the hand-curated, operator-authored task list / intent (`.ralph-overview/data.json`).
- **status / pipeline-state** = the watcher-derived runtime pipeline state
  (`.ralph-overview/generated/ralph-state.{js,json}`).
- Umbrella concept = "Ralph Roadmap"; the merged viewer surface = "the roadmap board."
- "What it is NOT": NOT an exec summary, NOT an architecture diagram, NOT a one-off status report —
  it is the living backlog + pipeline board.

### Implementation Strategy (ordered)
1. **Define-first, both repos, BEFORE any rename edit.** Add the one-line definition + two-part
   glossary + "what it is NOT" box to (a) codexu `AGENTS.md` and (b) the viewer
   (`overview-viewer/AGENTS.md` + the visible `App.tsx` header). This is the cheapest,
   highest-leverage deliverable and is the acceptance backbone.
2. **Living-surface prose rename (tiered).** Rename system references in the LIVING canonical docs
   first; treat historical/point-in-time docs as frozen (see Scope).
3. **Viewer visible text + additive npm aliases.**
4. **Optional additive technical aliases** (low-risk first: type aliases, dual env-var read; gate the
   medium-risk MCP dual-register + data-dir fallback on review).
5. **Version bump + CHANGELOG entry + codexu active-plugin-versions table** in lockstep with the
   submodule pointer bump.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Define-first glossary + "what it is NOT" box in codexu `AGENTS.md` and the viewer (both repos),
  landing BEFORE any rename.
- Human-facing prose rename of **living canonical docs** (Tier 1): codexu `AGENTS.md` (manual body),
  `README.md`, `plans/codexu-roadmap.md`, `docs/fork-roadmap.md`, `docs/submodule-rollback.md`,
  plugin `AGENTS.md`, viewer `AGENTS.md`. **NOTE (scope decision — needs operator sign-off, see Q6):**
  this is a deliberate **"living-docs-first" interpretation** of D-001's prose rename, NARROWER than
  D-001's literal ~1,880-occurrence sweep across all `plans/**` + `docs/**` + historical CHANGELOG.
  It is consistent with the brainstorm's core insight (most "overview" tokens live in frozen history
  no rename should reach) but it is a real narrowing, so the plan flags it explicitly rather than
  silently "inheriting D-001."
- "Roadmap bookkeeper" PROSE wording for the role, with the literal role id `overview-bookkeeper`
  preserved (runtime identifier).
- Viewer visible text + a11y strings: `<title>`, the `App.tsx` header, the `PipelineOverview`
  aria-label, the `TopLevelSurfaces` labels, the `Loading overview data…` string — and the viewer
  tests that assert those strings.
- Additive `roadmap*` npm script aliases in root `package.json` (existing keys retained;
  `sync-ralph-state` NOT aliased).
- OPTIONAL (Q4) low-risk additive technical aliases: `export type Roadmap* = Overview*`; env-var
  dual-read `RALPH_ROADMAP_PLUGIN_ROOT || RALPH_OVERVIEW_PLUGIN_ROOT` **via the plugin template**
  `templates/consumer-ralph-overview.mjs` (+ test) + codexu wrapper regen.
- Plugin version bump + new CHANGELOG entry + codexu active-plugin-versions table sync.

### Out of Scope
- **Destructive full rename (~575u):** renaming the `ralph-overview` plugin/marketplace/npm package,
  the `mcp__ralph-overview__*` namespace (as primary / drop-old), the `.ralph-overview/` data dir on
  disk, or the `Overview*` types as a hard rename. Future D-002 only, with a cross-machine migration
  runbook.
- **Renaming the live `.crews/` runtime role id `overview-bookkeeper`** and the `ralph-pipeline` crew
  name — runtime-state migration, deferred (Q2). Crew name is out per brainstorm invariant #1.
- **Frozen artifacts (Tier 3):** `.ralph/` history, `generated/**`, `tasks/INDEX.md`, completed
  point-in-time `plans/**` docs, historical CHANGELOG entries, past-version migration guides.
- **Higher-risk additive aliases by default:** dual-registering the 11 MCP tools and `.ralph-overview/`
  data-dir fallback resolution — recommend deferring (they add test/contract surface for no
  human-facing benefit); include only if the operator opts in (Q4).
- Renaming the `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` wrapper FILE or `overview.html` viewer FILENAME (bookmarked /
  package-keyed).

## Risk Areas
- **Semantic over-rename:** blind find-replace would corrupt technical identifiers, the generic word
  "overview", and historical artifacts. Mitigation: per-occurrence review; the acceptance criteria
  assert living-surface coverage, not count-to-zero.
- **Cross-repo coordination:** the toolkit (submodule) edit + version bump must land first; the codexu
  submodule pointer + active-plugin-versions table must move together in one codexu commit. A stale
  table OR a desynced marketplace-index version fails the CI invariant. Mitigation: the
  `ship-coordination` cluster (US-007) runs last with an explicit version-sync AC.
- **Same-plugin ship conflict with `ralph-overview-create-task-skill`:** both bump
  `plugin.json`/`CHANGELOG`/plugin `AGENTS.md`/skills → conflicting writes. Mitigation: **SERIALIZE
  at ship time** (one lands; the other rebases its topic branch onto the post-ship submodule main).
- **Contract breakage from accidental alias-as-primary OR partial dual-register:** additive aliases
  must be ADDITIVE (old names primary) and ALL-OR-NOTHING for the MCP set (a partial `roadmap.*`
  registration breaks `stdio-tools-list` parity). Mitigation: review asserts every `overview.*` tool +
  `Overview*` type still resolves; smoke `pnpm overview` + one
  `mcp__ralph-overview__overview_parallel_ready_tasks`.
- **Role-id mismatch:** if prose says "roadmap-bookkeeper" but runtime id stays `overview-bookkeeper`,
  readers may be confused. Mitigation: glossary pins both ("roadmap bookkeeper — role id
  `overview-bookkeeper`").

  manifests + 3 marketplace indexes are OWNED BY toolkit-surface (US-005's ship step); US-007 does NOT

  the codexu `AGENTS.md` active-plugin-versions table set to the toolkit-bumped value (+ the
  regenerated `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` if US-004 landed). Toolkit commit lands FIRST. Depends on
  codexu-surface + toolkit-surface; serializes at ship with `ralph-overview-create-task-skill`.

## Suggested Decomposition

Three clusters across two repos. The two SURFACE clusters are file-disjoint ACROSS repos (codexu
docs/scripts vs the `ai-developer-toolkit` submodule), so they can run as two parallel members (the
submodule worktree is git-index-disjoint from the codexu-primary checkout). The toolkit cluster
produces the bumped plugin version; the `ship-coordination` cluster runs LAST to record the codexu
submodule pointer + active-plugin-versions table together. Within each cluster, the define-first
story precedes its rename.

### Cluster: codexu-surface
- Stories: US-001, US-002, US-003
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`AGENTS.md` (US-001 inserts the glossary block, US-002 renames system
  references in the body — same file → serialize WITHIN the cluster)]; exclusive=[`README.md`,
  `plans/codexu-roadmap.md`, `docs/fork-roadmap.md`, `docs/submodule-rollback.md`, `package.json`];
  risk=medium (single-repo; US-001 must precede US-002 in `AGENTS.md`).
- `execution_mode` rationale: One serial cluster (single impl member) in the codexu-primary checkout.
  US-001→US-002 are ordered on `AGENTS.md`; US-003 (npm aliases) is independent and folds in. No
  submodule/contract dependency, so this can run in PARALLEL with toolkit-surface.

### Cluster: toolkit-surface
- Stories: US-005, US-006, US-004 (template side)
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None (file-disjoint from codexu-surface — different repo)
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[plugin `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`]; exclusive=[`overview-viewer/**`
  incl. its `__tests__`, `overview-mcp/**`, `scripts/lib/**`, `templates/consumer-ralph-overview.mjs`,
  `types.ts`, AND the version-bump files this cluster OWNS: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`,
  `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.github/plugin/plugin.json` + the 3 marketplace indexes]; risk=medium
  (lives in the `ai-developer-toolkit` SUBMODULE → submodule worktree; SERIALIZE at ship with
  `ralph-overview-create-task-skill`).
- `execution_mode` rationale: One serial cluster in a submodule worktree. Define-first (US-005 viewer
  block) precedes the US-005 viewer-text rename; US-006/US-004 are optional (Q4) and depend on US-005.
  US-004's codexu wrapper REGEN (a generated codexu file) folds into ship-coordination to avoid a
  codexu-index race with codexu-surface.

### Cluster: ship-coordination
- Stories: US-007 (+ US-004 codexu wrapper regen if Q4 landed)
- Phase: 2
- Depends on: codexu-surface, toolkit-surface
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[codexu `AGENTS.md` active-plugin-versions table — also touched by
  US-001/US-002 prose → must run AFTER codexu-surface]; exclusive=[the `ai-developer-toolkit`
  submodule gitlink (pointer) + `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` if US-004 landed]; risk=high (cross-repo
  pointer + version-table lockstep; CI invariant gate). NOTE: this cluster does NOT own the plugin
  manifests / marketplace indexes / CHANGELOG — those are bumped by toolkit-surface; here we only set
  the codexu table to that same value.
- `execution_mode` rationale: Runs AFTER both surface clusters so the codexu submodule pointer + the
  codexu `AGENTS.md` table reflect the toolkit-bumped plugin version; cannot parallelize with either.

Parallel handoff: `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan .ralph/jobs/overview-naming-rebrand/plan.md --parallel --suggested-decomposition .ralph/jobs/overview-naming-rebrand/suggested-decomposition.json`

> NOTE: `codexu-surface` and `toolkit-surface` are cross-repo file-disjoint and CAN run as two
> parallel members; `ship-coordination` must follow BOTH, and the toolkit cluster must SERIALIZE at
> ship time with the sibling task `ralph-overview-create-task-skill`. A serial run (single member,
> toolkit-surface → codexu-surface → ship-coordination) is the safest default given the cross-repo
> pointer/version lockstep and the same-plugin ship conflict.
